passport.title: Capture & fan-out (v2)
passport.description: Universal starter automation: it captures a message from any input channel and fans it out to every open output channel.
passport.author: architect

info.aiSummary: Maximal working v2 starter, domain-neutral. Every input channel (control panel, webhook, cron, public page, Telegram bot, user Telegram chat, email) normalizes its raw payload into one shared Message (text · source · at · title · optional lat/lng, _lib/message.ts); the middle validates it and derives the title; every output channel delivers it (dashboard, public page, calendar, analytics, map, email, Telegram ×2, vector memory, database, storage). Key-gated channels send for real when configured and skip honestly otherwise. Runs without AI.

howItWorks: A message enters through any input channel: the control panel form, an HTTP webhook, a scheduled tick, the public page form, the automation's Telegram bot, the user's own Telegram chat, or an inbound email.
The input node of that channel normalizes the raw payload into one shared Message: text, source, capture time, and coordinates when the channel provides them.
The middle validates the message — an empty capture honestly fails the run — and derives a short title from the first line of the text.

The success branch fans the message out to every open output at once: a dashboard row, a database record, a .txt file in local storage, a fact in vector memory, a calendar event, a per-channel analytics counter, a marker on the map when the message carries coordinates, and a post on the public page feed.
Key-gated deliveries (email, Telegram) send for real when their keys are configured in Settings, and otherwise skip honestly, naming the missing key in the run report.
Everything is deterministic: no AI runs at execution time, and the same input always takes the same path.

nodes.name: Incoming connector
nodes.description: Receives data from a node of ANOTHER automation — the door through which this automation joins a group. It is an OFFER, not a dependency: kept hidden, the automation runs perfectly well on its own.

info.aiSummary: Waits for data from a neighbouring automation; in a standalone automation it stays hidden.

function.name: receiveFromExternal
function.summary: Takes the payload handed over by another automation and names it for this one.
function.accepts: The payload as another automation handed it over.
function.returns: payload — the same value, named for this automation.

nodes.name: Control panel input
nodes.description: The default door: the owner's message typed into the control panel form.

info.aiSummary: Captures the control-panel form message (the default channel when a run names no source) and normalizes it into the shared Message. An empty message is refused at the door in ten languages; a run of another channel is passed through untouched.

function.name: receiveRequest
function.summary: Captures the control-panel form message and normalizes it into the shared Message shape.
function.accepts: The form fields of a run started from the control panel: text (required), optional lat/lng.
function.returns: Message fields merged into the context: text, source="control-panel", at, and lat/lng when given.

nodes.name: Webhook input
nodes.description: An external system calls in over HTTP.

info.aiSummary: Captures an HTTP push (POST api/run with source="webhook") and normalizes its JSON body into the shared Message: text ← text/message/payload, a structured payload is serialized rather than lost. Empty body — refused at the door. Input is push-only: nothing is polled.

function.name: receiveWebhook
function.summary: Normalizes an external HTTP push into the shared Message; a structured payload is serialized, never lost.
function.accepts: The JSON body of POST api/run with source="webhook": text, message or payload, optional lat/lng.
function.returns: Message fields merged into the context: text, source="webhook", at, and lat/lng when given.

nodes.name: Cron input
nodes.description: A scheduled tick fires it on a timer.

info.aiSummary: Turns a scheduler tick (POST api/run with source="cron") into a synthetic Message — the tick's own text or "Scheduled tick at <time>". The schedule itself is declared in the folder's cron.json when the owner enables the channel; the tick is a push, not a poll.

function.name: receiveCron
function.summary: Turns a scheduled tick into a synthetic Message so downstream work is exercised on a timer.
function.accepts: The tick pushed by the scheduler: optional text/message; nothing else is required.
function.returns: Message fields merged into the context: text (given or synthetic), source="cron", at.

nodes.name: Public Page input
nodes.description: A form or control on the automation own public page.

info.aiSummary: Captures a visitor's message from the automation's public page form (POST api/run with source="public-page") and normalizes it into the shared Message. Same normalization as the control panel; a separate channel so outputs can tell visitors from the owner.

function.name: receivePublicPage
function.summary: Captures a visitor's message from the public page form and normalizes it into the shared Message.
function.accepts: The form fields of a run with source="public-page": text (required), optional lat/lng.
function.returns: Message fields merged into the context: text, source="public-page", at, and lat/lng when given.

nodes.name: Telegram Bot input
nodes.description: A message sent to the automation own Telegram bot.

info.aiSummary: Captures a message sent to the automation's own Telegram bot: the listener pushes the update into api/run with source="telegram-bot", and the node understands both the raw Telegram shape ({message:{text,chat}}) and a pre-parsed text. The sender's chat id is kept in the context so a reply can reach exactly them. Live intake is gated on the channel keys.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_ID
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

function.name: receiveTelegramBot
function.summary: Normalizes a Telegram-bot update into the shared Message and keeps the sender's chat id for replies.
function.accepts: A pushed update with source="telegram-bot": raw {message:{text,chat:{id}}} or pre-parsed text.
function.returns: Message fields (text, source="telegram-bot", at) plus telegramChatId when the update names the chat.

nodes.name: User Telegram Chat input
nodes.description: A message read from the user own Telegram chat.

info.aiSummary: Captures a message from the user's own Telegram chat (linked natively via api/telegram/link): the listener pushes it into api/run with source="user-telegram-chat". Differs from telegram-bot by WHO writes — the user in their personal chat, not outsiders writing to the automation's bot. Live intake is gated on the channel keys.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

function.name: receiveUserTelegramChat
function.summary: Normalizes a message from the user's own linked Telegram chat into the shared Message.
function.accepts: A pushed update with source="user-telegram-chat": raw Telegram shape or pre-parsed text.
function.returns: Message fields (text, source="user-telegram-chat", at) plus telegramChatId when named.

nodes.name: Email input
nodes.description: Input for an email delivered to the automation's intake address.

info.aiSummary: Captures an inbound email: the provider pushes it into the api/inbound-email door (signature-checked), which starts a run with source="email". The body (or the subject when the body is empty) becomes the Message text; sender and subject stay in the context so the email output can reply to the sender. No mailbox polling — input is push-only.

envKeys.name: RESEND_API_KEY
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: RESEND_FROM_EMAIL
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: RESEND_INBOUND_SECRET
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

function.name: receiveEmail
function.summary: Normalizes an inbound email into the shared Message; sender and subject stay available for a reply.
function.accepts: The parsed letter pushed by api/inbound-email: from (required), subject, text.
function.returns: Message fields (text, source="email", at) plus emailFrom and emailSubject.

nodes.name: Logic
nodes.description: The middle — the deterministic work that turns the input into the output.

info.aiSummary: Validates and normalizes the captured Message: non-empty text (an empty capture fails the run in ten languages), collapsed whitespace, a title derived from the first line, stamped at/source. Deterministic, no keys, no AI — this throw is the real success/failure gate of the flow.

function.name: transformPayload
function.summary: Validates the captured message and derives its title; an empty capture honestly fails the run.
function.accepts: The Message fields put into the context by the input node of the run's channel.
function.returns: text · title · at · source — the normalized message every output node consumes.

nodes.name: Classify intent
nodes.description: The middle — labels the message with one or more intents (save/remind/recall/finance/place) so ONE automation can fan out to several branches, each self-gating on its flag. Hidden until a builder reveals it.

info.aiSummary: Intent classifier (step 308.0): sets ctx.intent (multi-flag from save|remind|recall|finance|place) via the passport model with deterministic parsing; attachment presence (photo→finance, location→place) is a hard, model-free signal; empty/failed → ['save'] so a message is never lost. Downstream action nodes self-gate with servesIntent(ctx,'<intent>') and pass through unchanged when not their intent (never null). No classifier present ⇒ ctx.intent absent ⇒ nodes act unconditionally (the simple capture→fan-out starter is unaffected). This is how v3 is ONE automation doing everything, incl. compound messages — v1's classify→fan-out in v2's linear engine. Node-skill of the middle library.

function.name: classifyIntent
function.summary: Labels the captured message with one or more intents so downstream branches can self-gate.
function.accepts: The captured message text plus optional attachment signals (ctx.photoFileId, ctx.location).
function.returns: intent: string[] — a subset of save|remind|recall|finance|place (never empty; defaults to ['save']).

nodes.name: Digitize money
nodes.description: The middle — turns a receipt photo or words about a payment into a structured money record (kind, amount, categories, summary). Hidden until a builder reveals it.

info.aiSummary: Money digitizer (step 308.3, v1 parity of parse-document): self-gates on the 'finance' intent; a receipt PHOTO → one vision call (askModelVision, Telegram getFile URL) extracts line items and their sum, WORDS → the same via askModel. Output is deterministic: strict JSON parsed and validated, categories forced through the fixed 10+10 preset (normalizeCategories drops hallucinated ids), amount null when unreadable. Three outcomes: own code (default); model unavailable/no key → soft degrade (financeUsed:false, never fabricates money); provider refusal (e.g. non-vision model) → throw. Node-skill of the middle library.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
envKeys.comment: Needed to fetch a receipt photo via getFile for the vision call.

function.name: digitizeMoney
function.summary: Turns a receipt photo or words about a payment into a structured money record.
function.accepts: ctx.text and/or ctx.photoFileId, gated on the 'finance' intent.
function.returns: finance: {kind, amount, categories[], summary, items[]} + financeUsed:true — OR financeUsed:false with financeError on soft degrade.

nodes.name: Store attachment
nodes.description: The middle — registers every incoming photo/document as a first-class object: downloads it, stores the bytes, gets a short vision description, writes a pending storage row. Hidden until revealed.

info.aiSummary: Attachment registrar (step 308.5, v1 parity of every-photo-is-first-class): NOT intent-gated — any photo is stored so nothing is lost. Downloads the Telegram file (downloadTelegramFile), saves the bytes to the folder object store (store.ts), takes a best-effort one-sentence vision description (askModelVision), writes a storage row status:'pending' (until linkAttachments 308.6 attaches it to records; the description later rides into the record's vector doc, 308.7, making the photo findable in memory). No photo → {}. Download/key failure → honest attachmentError, run does not fall. Node-skill of the middle library.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
envKeys.comment: Needed to download the attachment via getFile.

function.name: storeAttachment
function.summary: Registers every incoming photo/document: stores the bytes and a vision description as a pending object.
function.accepts: ctx.photoFileId (any intent).
function.returns: attachment: {fileKey, rowId, description} — OR {} when no photo, or attachmentError on unreachable file.

nodes.name: Link attachments
nodes.description: The middle — attaches photos/places to the records of a message burst in any order; picks up attachments left pending by earlier runs and late-attaches a lone photo to the latest bare record. Hidden until revealed.

info.aiSummary: Attachment linker (step 308.6, v1 parity of link-images): the many-to-many bond between attachments and records, order-independent. Works with creation-time linking — deliverDatabase/deliverVectorMemory read ctx.attachments and already carry this run's objects, so a compound message (interior photo + receipt + text) makes BOTH the note and the finance record hold BOTH photos. This node closes two cross-run cases: (1) it merges attachments left PENDING by earlier runs into ctx.attachments so this run's records carry them too, marking those storage rows linked; (2) when this run creates no record (e.g. only recall) it LATE-ATTACHES the attachments to the latest BARE record (empty storageIds) and flags it reindexNeeded so the photo's description enters its vector doc (308.7). Nowhere to attach → stays pending (nothing lost). Sets ctx.reindex when anything linked. Node-skill of the middle library.

function.name: linkAttachments
function.summary: Bonds attachments to the records of a burst in any order; picks up pending ones and late-attaches lone photos.
function.accepts: ctx.attachments (this run) + ctx.intent; reads pending storage rows and record tables.
function.returns: merged attachments + reindex flag, OR lateLinked target — OR {} when nothing to link.

nodes.name: Recall from memory
nodes.description: The middle — asks the vector memory (LightRAG) with the captured text and passes the ANSWER onward instead of the question.

info.aiSummary: Semantic recall over the automation's vector memory: the captured text becomes a question, LightRAG synthesizes an answer from the saved facts, and the answer replaces ctx.text so any output channel delivers it as an ordinary message (the original question is kept in ctx.question). Three honest outcomes, none of which fails the run: memory unreachable → a ten-language unavailable notice; an empty answer → a ten-language nothing-found notice with the query; an answer → the answer itself. Node-skill #1 of the middle library (step 307).

function.name: recallFromMemory
function.summary: Asks the vector memory with the captured text and passes the synthesized answer onward; degrades honestly when memory is unreachable or empty.
function.accepts: The normalized message text — the user's question to the saved facts.
function.returns: text (the answer or an honest notice) · title · question · at · source.

nodes.name: AI transform
nodes.description: The middle — thinks with the automation's chosen model (passport.ai): runs the captured text through an instruction and passes the result onward.

info.aiSummary: Runs the captured text through the model selected in the passport (passport.ai) by an instruction (ctx.aiInstruction, default: a concise fact-and-date-preserving summary) and passes the result onward as ctx.text; the original is kept in ctx.original. Native call, no SDK (folder law 0). Soft-degrade: model unavailable (no key/network) or refused → the full original text is kept and the run continues (aiUsed=false, aiError set) — losing information is worse than losing the summary. Node-skill #2 of the middle library (step 307).

function.name: aiTransform
function.summary: Thinks with the passport model over the captured text by an instruction; degrades to the untouched original when the model is unavailable or refuses.
function.accepts: The normalized message text plus an optional ctx.aiInstruction.
function.returns: text (the model result or the untouched original) · original · title · at · source · aiUsed.

nodes.name: Parse date
nodes.description: The middle — extracts the reminder date-and-time from the captured text into ctx.when (ISO), or flags ctx.needsWhen when there is none. The message text is left unchanged.

info.aiSummary: Extracts a single reminder datetime from the captured text via the passport model, then validates the answer DETERMINISTICALLY (strict ISO or the word none; any garbage = needsWhen). Result: ctx.when (ISO) or ctx.needsWhen=true; the text is untouched (this is preparation for the calendar output). Server-local timezone (the model gets the server now). Model unavailable/refused → needsWhen (safer to ask when? than to set a wrong time). Node-skill #3 of the middle library (step 307).

function.name: parseDate
function.summary: Extracts the reminder datetime from the captured text into ctx.when, or flags ctx.needsWhen; deterministic validation, server-local timezone.
function.accepts: The normalized message text (a reminder request in free wording).
function.returns: when (ISO) and needsWhen=false, OR needsWhen=true (with optional dateError). The text is unchanged.

nodes.name: Ask address
nodes.description: The middle — for a 'place' with no coordinates, honestly asks the user to share the location or send an address (the device has no auto-geolocation). Hidden until revealed.

info.aiSummary: Address request (step 308.4, v1 parity): self-gates on the 'place' intent. Coordinates present (user shared a point/venue → carried in lat/lng by the input node) → stays silent ({}), deliverMap places the marker. No coordinates → needsAddress:true and a 10-language question in text so the reply node asks the user (same pattern as the calendar 'when?'). Deterministic, no model, never fabricates a point. Node-skill of the middle library.

function.name: askAddress
function.summary: For a place without coordinates, asks the user to share the location or send an address.
function.accepts: ctx.lat/ctx.lng (optional) gated on the 'place' intent.
function.returns: {} when coordinates are present; needsAddress:true + a question in text when they are not.

nodes.name: Hook gate
nodes.description: The middle — self-gates the run on this automation's trigger phrase so several automations can share one chat without an N-way router.

info.aiSummary: Deterministic hook self-gate (step 307.7): reads trigger phrases from ctx.hookPhrases and passes the run on ONLY if the captured text starts with one of them (normalizing case, ё/е, whitespace), putting the tail after the phrase into ctx.text and the phrase into ctx.hookPhrase. A foreign phrase returns null — a lawful stop (this run is not mine). No phrases set → the gate is open. No AI. This is how a GROUP of automations shares one personal chat, since v2 has no N-way router by design. Node-skill #6 of the middle library.

function.name: hookGate
function.summary: Passes the run on only when the captured text starts with one of this automation's trigger phrases; a foreign phrase stops the run cleanly.
function.accepts: The captured message text plus ctx.hookPhrases (this automation's trigger phrases).
function.returns: text (the payload after the phrase) · hookPhrase · hookMatched — OR null (foreign phrase, lawful stop).

nodes.name: If success
nodes.description: The branch taken when the middle produced a result — the flow continues to the output.

info.aiSummary: The success branch: holds only when the normalized message carries non-empty text — then the flow fans out to every open output. When it does not hold, the node returns null and the run stops lawfully (the middle's throw is the loud failure; this is the quiet gate).

function.name: ifSuccess
function.summary: Lets the flow through to the outputs only when a non-empty normalized message exists.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) produced by the middle.
function.returns: The same context when the branch holds; null (a lawful stop) when it does not.

nodes.name: If failure
nodes.description: The branch taken when the middle could not produce a result — the flow ends here.

info.aiSummary: The failure branch: a named dead end on the canvas. The real failure has already stopped the run with the middle's throw (empty capture, refused input), so the function is an honest no-op — the node exists so the owner SEES where a failed run ends.

function.name: ifFailure
function.summary: Ends the flow when the middle produced no message; the canvas shows where a failed run stops.
function.accepts: The failure reported by the middle of the flow.
function.returns: Nothing — a failure branch ends the flow.

nodes.name: Compose reply
nodes.description: The middle composes ONE coherent, formatted, localized reply to the user from the run structured result. Hidden until revealed.

info.aiSummary: Reply composer (step 308, conversational contract _instructions/replies.md): instead of the user getting the raw ctx.text of whichever node acted last, this ONE node reads the structured result of the run (noteSummary, finance, when/needsWhen+remindText, placeOutcome, recallAnswer, showHelp) and builds a single coherent, emoji-formatted, localized reply into ctx.reply. A compound message becomes one reply about everything. An unrecognized message or /start or what-can-you-do returns the capability introduction. deliverUserTelegramChat sends ctx.reply. Not intent-gated. Node-skill of the middle library.

function.name: composeReply
function.summary: Builds one coherent localized reply to the user from the run structured result.
function.accepts: the run context (noteSummary, finance, when, placeOutcome, recallAnswer, showHelp, intent).
function.returns: reply, one formatted message; the capability list for /start or an unrecognized message.

nodes.name: Converse
nodes.description: The middle, role conversation, talks to the human with the model by the Assistant-tab behavior script, with dialogue memory. Hidden until revealed.

info.aiSummary: Conversational boundary (step 309, role=conversation): a distinct KIND of work, not computing over data but COMFORTABLE DIALOGUE with the human, which is by nature the model's job. Builds ctx.reply by thinking with the model over the Assistant-tab behavior instruction + the per-chat dialogue buffer + Q&A few-shot examples + the run's structured result. No model/key -> deterministic fallback composeReply (proven). The role makes it first-class and unmissable in the frozen template. Node-skill of the middle library.

function.name: converse
function.summary: Builds one comfortable localized reply to the user with the model, by the behavior script and dialogue memory.
function.accepts: the run structured result + ctx.telegramChatId; reads the Assistant tab config and the chat buffer.
function.returns: reply, one comfortable message; deterministic composeReply fallback when no model.

nodes.name: Dashboard output
nodes.description: A row in the automation dashboard's history table.

info.aiSummary: Writes the captured message into the dashboard history table: one row per successful run — date · source · title · text (folder-local rows store, _lib/rows.ts).

function.name: deliverResult
function.summary: Writes one history row per successful run: date, source channel, title and text of the message.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) carried by the success branch.
function.returns: rowId — the id of the history row written to the dashboard.

nodes.name: Outgoing connector
nodes.description: Hands the result over to a node of ANOTHER automation — the door out into a group.

info.aiSummary: Passes the WHOLE shared Message to a neighbouring automation — the far side receives the same contract every channel speaks. Provable only inside a group of automations, so in the standalone starter it stays hidden.

function.name: handToExternal
function.summary: Hands the whole shared Message over to the automation waiting on the other side.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source, optional lat/lng) of the success branch.
function.returns: handover — the Message object, handed to another automation.

nodes.name: Public Page output
nodes.description: A page on the automation own website.

info.aiSummary: Publishes the captured message to the public page feed: a row in the public-page table (date · source · title · text), read through api/rows?table=public-page. The node delivers the feed's DATA; how to render it is the page component's choice.

function.name: deliverPublicPage
function.summary: Appends the message to the public page feed table so the page can show it.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) carried by the success branch.
function.returns: publicPageRowId — the id of the feed row written.

nodes.name: Calendar output
nodes.description: An event on the automation calendar.

info.aiSummary: Places the captured message as a calendar event. The event time is ctx.when (parsed by parseDate) when present, else the capture moment; ctx.needsWhen (no date found) is an honest ten-language "when?" refusal — no row is created. To make an occurrence actually deliver, it sets an ACTIVE integration on the SOURCE telegram channel (asked in Telegram → reminded in Telegram); api/calendar-tick then delivers it (step 307.6).

function.name: deliverCalendar
function.summary: Creates a calendar event titled like the message at its capture moment.
function.accepts: The captured message; optionally ctx.when (parsed date from parseDate) and ctx.needsWhen.
function.returns: calendarRowId and calendarWhen (ISO); refuses in ten languages when needsWhen is set.

nodes.name: Analytics output
nodes.description: A chart in the automation analytics.

info.aiSummary: Keeps per-channel counters of captured messages: one analytics-table row per input channel (metric "captured" · source · count · lastAt); every successful run increments its channel's counter through the journal store (the edit history keeps itself).

function.name: deliverAnalytics
function.summary: Increments the captured-messages counter of the run's input channel in the analytics table.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) carried by the success branch.
function.returns: analyticsCount — the channel's counter value after this run.

nodes.name: Map output
nodes.description: A marker on the automation map.

info.aiSummary: Puts a marker on the automation map: a row in the map table (date · title · source · lat · lng). Coordinates are optional in the contract, so a message without lat/lng is delivered honestly-degraded — a skip with the reason in the run context, never an invented point.

function.name: deliverMap
function.summary: Writes a map marker at the message's lat/lng; without coordinates it skips honestly with a reason.
function.accepts: The normalized message; lat/lng when the input channel captured them.
function.returns: mapDelivery — "marker <id> at lat,lng" or "skipped: …" naming the missing coordinates.

nodes.name: Email output
nodes.description: An email the automation sends out.

info.aiSummary: Sends the captured message as an email via the shared transport (_lib/transport.ts, Resend). Recipient by explicitness: emailTo from the flow → the inbound sender (an honest reply) → RESEND_TO_EMAIL. An unconfigured channel (no key / no recipient) skips honestly with the reason; a refusal from the service with live keys throws.

envKeys.name: RESEND_API_KEY
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: RESEND_FROM_EMAIL
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: RESEND_TO_EMAIL
envKeys.comment: Optional owner address for fan-out letters; without it and without emailTo/emailFrom in the flow the node skips honestly.

function.name: deliverEmail
function.summary: Emails the message via Resend; unconfigured channel skips honestly, a service refusal throws.
function.accepts: The normalized message plus an optional recipient (emailTo, or emailFrom of an inbound letter).
function.returns: emailDelivery — "sent <id> to <address>" or "skipped: …" naming what is not configured.

nodes.name: Telegram Bot output
nodes.description: A message sent through the automation own Telegram bot.

info.aiSummary: Sends the captured message through the automation's own Telegram bot into its working chat (TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_ID) via the shared transport. Unconfigured channel (no token/chat) skips honestly with the reason; a Telegram refusal with live keys throws.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_ID
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

function.name: deliverTelegramBot
function.summary: Sends the message through the automation's bot; unconfigured channel skips honestly, a refusal throws.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) carried by the success branch.
function.returns: telegramBotDelivery — "sent <message id>" or "skipped: …" naming the missing key.

nodes.name: User Telegram Chat output
nodes.description: A message written into the user own Telegram chat.

info.aiSummary: Writes the captured message into the USER'S personal Telegram chat (linked via api/telegram/link → TELEGRAM_USER_CHAT_ID; a chat id carried by the run itself wins — an honest reply to the sender). Same bot token as the bot channel: one service, one key. Unconfigured → honest skip; a refusal with live keys throws.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
envKeys.comment: Declared by the channel; the api/env door checks its live presence.

envKeys.name: TELEGRAM_USER_CHAT_ID
envKeys.comment: The user's personal chat, linked natively via api/telegram/link (step 296); a run's own telegramChatId wins over it.

function.name: deliverUserTelegramChat
function.summary: Writes the message into the user's linked personal chat; unconfigured channel skips honestly.
function.accepts: The normalized message plus an optional telegramChatId carried by the run.
function.returns: userTelegramDelivery — "sent <id> to <chat>" or "skipped: …" naming what is missing.

nodes.name: Vector memory output
nodes.description: Output to the agent vector memory (LightRAG).

info.aiSummary: Remembers the captured message as a FACT: ingests it into LightRAG (folder-own call _lib/memory.ts, provenance projects/other/frozen-template-v-2?channel=<source>&record=<unique> — the unique tail is the uniqueness law) and writes a visible row into the vector-memory table (name · content · trackId). Service unreachable → honest skip; service refusal → throw.

envKeys.name: LIGHTRAG_URL
envKeys.comment: Optional — the node defaults to http://127.0.0.1:9621 (the platform memory service); an unreachable service degrades to an honest skip.

envKeys.name: LIGHTRAG_API_KEY
envKeys.comment: Optional — sent as X-API-Key when the memory service requires one for writes.

function.name: deliverVectorMemory
function.summary: Ingests the message into LightRAG with unique provenance and records the fact row; unreachable service skips honestly.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) carried by the success branch.
function.returns: vectorMemoryDelivery ("remembered <track id>" or "skipped: …") and vectorRowId of the fact row.

nodes.name: Database output
nodes.description: If you activate this node, you can store and retrieve data in your own local database. If you also use object storage or a vector database, the local database keeps the links that locate those objects, too.

info.aiSummary: Writes the captured message as a record of the automation's own local database: a database-table row (name · text · source · date · storageIds · vectorIds). By the stores law the record HOLDS LINKS to the neighbouring stores: the vector fact's row id lands in vectorIds when the memory output ran earlier in the same fan-out.

function.name: deliverDatabase
function.summary: Writes a database record of the message, linking the vector fact written earlier in the same run.
function.accepts: The normalized message plus vectorRowId when the vector-memory output already ran.
function.returns: databaseRowId — the id of the database record written.

nodes.name: Storage output
nodes.description: If you activate this node, you can save and use media files and documents related to this automation in your own local storage.

info.aiSummary: Saves the captured message as a .txt FILE in the folder's object storage (_lib/store.ts → _data/runtime/objects/) and writes the storage-table row holding the link (fileKey · name · kind "text" · size) — bytes live in the store, the row holds the reference: the database→storage link of the stores law.

function.name: deliverStorage
function.summary: Saves the message as a .txt object and records the storage row holding its fileKey link.
function.accepts: The normalized message (text · title · at · source) carried by the success branch.
function.returns: storageFileKey and storageRowId — the object's key and the row that links to it.

info.aiSummary: Launch panel: one longtext message field declared in the core (data.params), the run button into api/run, the run report. The default input door of the capture→fan-out starter.

cases.title: Capture a message from any channel
cases.text: I want to send a message through any input channel — the control panel, an HTTP webhook, a scheduled tick, the public page form, the automation's Telegram bot, my own Telegram chat or an inbound email — and have the automation capture it as one common message.

cases.title: Fan the message out to every output
cases.text: I want every captured message delivered everywhere at once — a dashboard row, a database record, a .txt file in storage, a fact in vector memory, a calendar event, an analytics counter, a map marker when the message carries coordinates, a post on the public page, an email and a Telegram message — so every delivery pattern of the platform is real and explorable.

versions.summary: Step 300: the stock-price demo became the domain-neutral capture→fan-out starter. All 7 input channels and all 11 output channels carry real functions speaking one Message contract (text · source · at · title · lat/lng); key-gated deliveries skip honestly when unconfigured; the stock domain, the demo warning and the v1 ?view=public surface were removed.

Step 300 freeze: after live proofs on the server (all four key-free channels ran end-to-end; vector memory ingested with real track ids; storage/database/calendar/analytics/map rows written; key-gated channels reported honest skips) every node and edge was hidden and the lifecycle set to frozen-template. Real, proven functions remain behind every hidden door, ready to be unhidden.
